sentence: This project studies how hematopoietic stem cells with mutations expand into clonal populations, using mitochondrial lineage tracing in aging and a familial platelet disorder.
This project builds a data and technology system that uses machine learning and mobile health tools to support mobility and independence in older adults.
This project tries to find out how certain RNAs are moved to the midbody, an organelle needed for cell division, using experiments and computer methods.
This project uses placental cells from normal and Trisomy 21-affected placentas to find cell defects that underlie placental dysfunction.
This project provides computer and statistics support for vision researchers, including analysis of large datasets from single-cell sequencing and other sequencing methods.
This project tries to find out what a second stem cell population does as cancer develops and what weaknesses in it could be targeted.
This project studies how oncogene amplification leads to genome instability and therapy resistance in cancer cells, and tests ways to reduce that instability.
This project tries to find out how the protein tau misfolds and clumps together in human neurons, depending on its sequence and its cellular environment.
This project studies how polychlorinated biphenyls disrupt communication between adipocytes and macrophages, leading to inflammation and dysfunction in adipose tissue.
This project measures brain activity in a mouse model of Parkinson’s Disease to learn how dopamine replacement therapy helps movement but also causes involuntary movements.
This project tests whether doing aerobic exercise right before cognitive behavior therapy sessions makes the therapy work better for depression.
This project studies reproductive biology and reproductive disorders through basic research and clinical investigation.
This project studies how metabolites and proteins released by gut bacteria change how drugs are absorbed and metabolized.
This project builds an open-source platform where researchers can share, view and analyze digital images of brain slides for Alzheimer's Disease research.
This project studies how 3D wall enhancement and geometric features relate to the growth in volume of intracranial aneurysms.
This project tries to find out how benzalkonium chloride harms the corneal epithelium and tests ways to protect human corneal epithelial cells.
This project studies the genomic profiles of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma linked to Epstein-Barr virus in people with immunodeficiency.
This project builds a resource to test imaging methods that measure how well therapy works on patient-derived tumors implanted in mice.
This project uses qualitative methods to explore what adolescents and adults in Uganda know and think about air pollution and health.
This project studies how environmental pollutants that build up in adipose tissue disrupt endothelial cells and adipocytes and contribute to vascular disease.
